deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is pp. 5-6 of a numbered sub-sequence of the 'Systèmes de pseudo-droites' notes. The previous page defined an orientation ω of a 1-dimensional arrangement as a choice, for every non-concurrent triple I, of an orientation ω_I of the corresponding 'octahedral' graph. It then stated that the functor sending a combinatorial map (cellular decomposition of the projective plane given by a pseudo-line arrangement) to its oriented 1-skeleton (K, (D_i), ω) is fully faithful. This page backs up to give the precise definition of the target objects.

Definition (modern language).
- K is a finite graph, possibly with multiple edges.
- (D_i)_{i∈J} is a finite family of subgraphs, each a cycle ('polygonal sub-complex').
- The edge set of K is partitioned by the D_i: every edge lies in exactly one D_i.
- For i≠j, D_i ∩ D_j is exactly one vertex. The image seems to read 'un sommet et un seul'; the transcription's 'au plus' is doubtful.
- Every vertex lies on at least two of the D_i.
- A first condition, excluding isolated vertices, is struck out because it is implied.
- The data is called a 1-dimensional arrangement of pseudo-lines provided ⋂_i D_i = ∅.

The last condition excludes the degenerate 'pinceau' (pencil): a bouquet of loops (monogons) all passing through one common vertex. Under the pairwise-one-point hypothesis it gives a non-concurrent triple I ⊂ J, |I| = 3, with ⋂_{i∈I} D_i = ∅. Proof: take i, j meeting at s; some k misses s.

For I ⊂ J, K_I is the graph which is topologically the union of the D_i (i∈I), with vertices only at the pairwise intersections. In the relevant case (|I| = 3, no common point), K_I has:
- 3 vertices (the pairwise intersection points);
- 6 edges, each D_i being a 2-gon through its two intersection points.

This is the 1-skeleton of the decomposition of RP² by three lines into four triangles, i.e. the antipodal quotient of the octahedron. Hence 'graphe octaédral', and one can speak of an orientation of this graph: a binary choice of which edge-triples bound the four triangles, equivalently a choice of rotation system realizing it.

Two margin notes (largely illegible) appear to say:
- the polygons D_i have length ≥ 2, i.e. there are no monogons outside the pencil case;
- K_I is itself an arrangement exactly when ⋂_{i∈I} D_i = ∅.

What this serves. The programme is to reconstruct the 2-dimensional map 𝔛 (a cellular decomposition of RP² by pseudo-lines) from purely 1-dimensional data plus triple orientations. The next page does this by producing, at each vertex s, the pair of mutually inverse cyclic orders on the arcs (equivalently oriented pseudo-lines) through s, and parallel-transport bijections ψ_a along arcs with ψ_{a⁻¹} = ψ_a⁻¹. The general theory of maps (rotation systems) then yields a cellular embedding. This is a combinatorial-maps proof that an arrangement in RP² is determined by its incidence graph plus local chirality of triples: essentially the statement that a (not necessarily simple) rank-3 oriented matroid, up to reorientation, is determined by its triple signs and determines the cell complex.
errors: Indexing inconsistency: the family is introduced as (D_i)_{i∈I}, later indexed by J, with I reused for subsets of J.

If the transcribed 'au plus un sommet' were Grothendieck's intent, disjoint D_i would be allowed. That contradicts pseudo-line behaviour in RP² and the subsequent use of 'the' intersection points; the image supports 'exactly one'.

'Graphe octogonal gradué' in the machine transcription should be 'graphe octaédral' (consistent with p.39); the 3-vertex, 6-edge graph is octahedral only via the antipodal double cover, which is implicit.

ideas.what: Purely 1-dimensional axiomatization of a pseudo-line arrangement: a graph with an edge-partition into cycles, pairwise meeting in exactly one vertex, every vertex on ≥ 2 cycles, not all concurrent
ideas.modern_name: Incidence/1-skeleton description of a (non-simple) projective pseudo-line arrangement; underlying rank-3 matroid with its arrangement graph
ideas.usually_credited_to: Levi (1926), Grünbaum (1972, Arrangements and Spreads); matroid side Folkman–Lawrence (1978)

ideas.what: Existence of a non-concurrent triple whenever the lines are not a pencil
ideas.modern_name: Trivial rank-3 fact (an arrangement not of rank 2 has a basis triple)

ideas.what: Local orientation datum on each non-concurrent triple (orientation of the 'octahedral' graph K_I) as the extra structure needed to recover the 2-dimensional map
ideas.modern_name: Chirotope / triple orientations up to reorientation; Knuth's CC-systems; Folkman–Lawrence topological representation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folkman–Lawrence 1978, Lawrence 1982, Bland–Las Vergnas 1978, Goodman–Pollack, Knuth 1992 (Axioms and Hulls)
ideas.where_published: Not known in published texts; Esquisse d'un programme discusses combinatorial maps, but explicit pseudo-line material there is unsure

missed.claim: Grothendieck frames the oriented-matroid/arrangement correspondence (unoriented lines, non-simple arrangements allowed) as a fully faithful functor from combinatorial maps to oriented 1-dimensional arrangements. Reconstruction is via the theory of maps: cyclic orders at vertices plus transport bijections along arcs, a kind of flat 'local system' of cyclic orders. This categorical/maps-theoretic formulation, rather than chirotope axioms, is not the standard one in the oriented matroid literature, though the underlying mathematics is known.
missed.quote: On dit alors que (K,(D_i)_{i∈I}) est un arrangement 1-dimensionnel de ps. droites ... K_I est un graphe octaédral ... d'orientation de ce graphe
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly historical interest: it shows Grothendieck independently developing oriented-matroid-type ideas in the language of combinatorial maps (dessins). The mathematical content is covered by Folkman–Lawrence and Knuth.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful definition page. The content corresponds to known oriented-matroid/pseudo-line theory (rank 3, up to reorientation). Its interest is the independent maps-theoretic framing by Grothendieck, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'ont en commun {+au plus+} un sommet et un seul' — the image appears to read 'ont en commun un sommet et un seul' (exactly one).
'{+N.B.+} pourvu que l'intersection des D_i soit vide' is more likely 'Supposons que l'intersection des D_i soit vide'.
'K ne est pas simplement les "jointes"' should read 'que K ne soit pas simplement le "pinceau" de monogones (ou "boucles")'.
'réunion de cercles pas ayant un sommet commun' is more likely 'réunion de [monogones/boucles] ayant un sommet commun' (the pencil case).
'de cardinal ≥ 3' is probably 'de cardinal 3'; 'n'aient pas un commun' should be 'n'aient pas de point commun'.
'moins un point commun sommets que les intersections' should read 'n'ayant comme sommets que les intersections (deux à deux) des D_i'.
'intimes (cad I=3,)' should be 'Dans le cas qui nous intéresse (càd card I = 3, ⋂ D_i = ∅)'.
'graphe octogonal gradué' should be 'graphe octaédral', and 'orientation de ce graphe octaédral' likewise.
